summary: The reader has an undergraduate computer science education: asymptotic analysis, recursion and divide-and-conquer recurrences, basic discrete mathematics (modular arithmetic, primes, Chinese remainder theorem, permutations, sets), and introductory linear algebra (vectors, matrices, invertible maps, subspaces, triangular matrices, Gaussian elimination). They know binary arithmetic, schoolbook and Karatsuba multiplication, and basic Turing machines with tapes. They have not studied abstract algebra beyond basics, the FFT in depth, Schönhage-Strassen, Nussbaumer transforms, or fast multitape tape-programming techniques; those are explained by the wiki.

known.name: Logarithms and iterated logarithms
known.gloss: The base-2 logarithm lg n is the exponent to which 2 is raised to get n, and lg lg n applies it twice.

known.name: Binary representation of integers
known.gloss: A nonnegative integer below 2^n is written as a string of n bits, the coefficients of its powers of 2.

known.name: Positional radix notation
known.gloss: An integer is written as a sum of digits times powers of a base, so splitting into digits and recombining with carries are inverse operations.

known.name: Schoolbook and Karatsuba multiplication
known.gloss: Schoolbook multiplication takes quadratic time in the bit length, and Karatsuba's divide-and-conquer multiplication improves this to a power below 2.

known.name: Recursion and divide-and-conquer recurrences
known.gloss: Running time of a recursive algorithm is described by a recurrence that is solved by unrolling levels or by the master theorem.

known.name: Modular arithmetic
known.gloss: Integers are compared and combined modulo n, so indices and values wrap around cyclically.

known.name: Primes and coprimality
known.gloss: A prime has no divisors besides 1 and itself, and integers with gcd 1 are coprime.

known.name: Chinese remainder theorem
known.gloss: For pairwise coprime moduli, residues modulo each determine a unique residue modulo their product, giving an isomorphism of Z/(m1...mk) with the product of the Z/mi.

known.name: Permutations and bijections
known.gloss: A permutation is a bijective rearrangement of a list of positions, and sorting realizes one.

known.name: Vectors, matrices and linear maps
known.gloss: Linear maps are represented by matrices acting on coefficient vectors, compose by matrix product, and are undone by inverses.

known.name: Subspaces, dimension and linear independence
known.gloss: A subspace is a subset of a vector space closed under linear combination, with a dimension given by the size of a basis.

known.name: Triangular matrices and Gaussian elimination
known.gloss: Triangular matrices have zeros on one side of the diagonal, and Gaussian elimination factors or inverts matrices by elementary row operations.

known.name: Bitwise operations and XOR
known.gloss: XOR adds bits modulo 2, and fields of bits in a binary address can be read and modified independently.

known.name: Cartesian products and multidimensional arrays
known.gloss: A multidimensional array is indexed by tuples from a product of finite sets, and can be laid out linearly by an ordering of indices.

known.name: Sets and subsets
known.gloss: A subset consists of chosen elements of a ground set, and the number of subsets of a given size is counted combinatorially.

known.name: Rationals, rounding and error bounds
known.gloss: Real approximations are rounded to the nearest integer, which is exact when the total error is strictly below 1/2 and is bounded by summing individual errors.

known.name: Dyadic rationals and fixed-point numbers
known.gloss: A dyadic rational has a power of 2 as denominator and is stored as an integer scaled by a power of 2.

known.name: Two's complement and signed integers
known.gloss: Negative integers are stored in binary through a sign convention such as two's complement, with offsets or sign bits.

known.name: Basic ring and group structure
known.gloss: A commutative ring has addition and multiplication satisfying the usual laws, and it can be quotiented by a relation such as y^r = -1.

known.name: Euler's formula and primitive roots of unity
known.gloss: The number e^{2 pi i/N} is a primitive N-th root of unity of modulus 1, and its powers are the points evenly spaced on the unit circle.

known.name: Fast Fourier transform for power-of-two length
known.gloss: The radix-2 FFT computes a length-2^k transform in O(N log N) arithmetic operations by splitting recursively into half-length transforms and combining with butterflies.

known.name: Gaussian function
known.gloss: The function exp(-pi x^2) is a rapidly decaying bell-shaped function whose tails give small approximation errors.

known.name: Time and space as functions of input size
known.gloss: Algorithms are compared by worst-case step counts as functions of input length, and a subroutine is used as a black box with its running time.

known.name: Tape head movement and sequential access
known.gloss: A Turing machine head moves one cell per step, so scanning a tape costs time proportional to its length and random access is not free.
